info.title: smolvm API
info.description: smolvm API for managing machines and images.

delete.summary:
Remove a cache base from this server: a base a failed publish left behind,
or one whose cache disk was deleted. Refused while a machine here is
attached to it. Removing a base that is not here succeeds, so a retry is
safe; a base that is needed again is fetched from its source.

204.description: Cache base removed, or was not here

400.description: Invalid name, or cache disks disabled

409.description: A machine is attached to the base

post.description: This executes directly in the VM (not in a container).

200.description: Command executed; with `stream`, its output as Server-Sent Events

get.summary: Interactive session over a WebSocket.
get.description:
The client connects a WebSocket; binary frames are forwarded to the
command's stdin and its output is sent back as binary frames. A JSON text
frame `{"type":"resize","cols":N,"rows":N}` resizes the terminal. When the
command exits, a final text frame `{"type":"exit","code":N}` is sent before
the socket closes. Closing the socket ends the session, and the command is
killed.

Query parameters: `cmd` is the program and each `arg` one argument to it;
`tty` chooses between a PTY (the default, which merges stderr into stdout)
and pipes.

With `tty=false` stdin is written with backpressure and nothing is ever
dropped: the WebSocket is read only as fast as the command takes its input.
Standard output is the binary frames, byte for byte. Standard error is
reported as text frames `{"type":"stderr","data":"..."}` (lossily decoded
as UTF-8), so it never mixes into the stream.

Image machines run the program in their persistent-overlay container (the
same filesystem `exec` uses); plain machines run it directly in the VM.

parameters.name: cmd
parameters.description: Program to run (the machine's shell when absent)

parameters.name: arg
parameters.description: One argument to the program, repeated in order

parameters.name: tty
parameters.description: Run on a pseudo-terminal (the default) or on pipes

101.description: Switching to the WebSocket terminal protocol

500.description: The machine could not be started

post.summary: Execute a command with streaming output (Server-Sent Events).
post.description:
Returns real-time stdout/stderr as SSE events. Useful for long-running
commands where buffering the entire output is impractical.

409.description: Machine not running and autoStart is false

get.summary: List the exec sessions on a machine.

post.summary: Start a command the node owns.
post.description:
Answers once the command is running (or failed to start), with the output
from offset 0 after waiting up to `waitSecs`. A start whose `execId` the
node already has answers with that session, so a client may retry a start
whose answer it never got without running the command twice.

200.description: Already started by an earlier request with this execId

409.description: The execId names a different or spent command, or the machine is not running and autoStart is false

503.description: The node holds as many exec sessions as it may

get.summary: Read an exec session's output.
get.description:
Returns the output after `after` (at most `max` bytes), waiting up to
`wait` seconds for some when there is none yet. `after` acknowledges every
byte before it. Read again with `after` = the answer's `next` until `done`.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
Return output from this offset. It also acknowledges every byte before
it, which the node then drops. Default 0.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description:
Wait up to this many seconds (at most 60) for output past `after` or
the exit. Default 0.

parameters.name: max
parameters.description: Most output bytes in the answer.

400.description: Offset beyond the end of the output

404.description: No such exec on this machine

delete.summary: Kill an exec session's command if it runs, and forget the session.

404.description: No such exec on this machine

get.summary: Attach to an exec session over a WebSocket (see the module docs).

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Resume output from this offset, acknowledging what precedes it

400.description: The offset is beyond the session's output

post.summary: Resize an exec session's terminal.

404.description: No such exec on this machine

409.description: The session has no terminal, or ended

post.summary: Write one sequenced stdin frame to an interactive exec session.
post.description:
Answers with the last frame applied. A frame already applied is answered
without applying it again; a frame after a missing one is not applied, and
the answer's `stdinApplied` says where to resend from.

404.description: No such exec on this machine

409.description: Stdin is closed, or the session takes none

503.description: The command did not take its input in time; nothing applied

get.summary: Download a file, or list a directory, from a machine.
get.description:
A file returns its contents as a raw byte stream. A directory returns its
entries as JSON, so a caller exploring a tree does not have to know in
advance which paths are files, and does not have to guess names and eat a
404 for each miss.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: File or directory path inside the VM

200.description: File contents (application/octet-stream) or, for a directory, an `entries` array of name/kind/size (application/json)

put.summary: Upload a file to a machine.
put.description:
Writes the request body as a file at the specified path inside the VM.
Creates parent directories automatically. `?mode=`, `?uid=` and `?gid=` set
the file's permission bits and owner (see [`UploadOptions`]).

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: File path inside the VM (e.g., workspace/script.py)

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Permission bits in octal, such as `0755` or `644`.

Publish a stopped machine's cache disk, its base with everything the
machine wrote over it, as a new self-contained base in the server's cache
disk directory. The new base appears whole or not at all, and the old one is
left as it is, so machines still on it are unaffected.

get.summary:
List the machine's egress denials — outbound connects and sendtos its

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of events to return (newest kept). Default 200.

put.summary:
Replace a machine's environment. A stopped machine takes it at its next
start; a running one gives it to every command started from now on, since
each command reads the machine's environment from its record. A process
already running keeps the environment it started with.

409.description: Machine is starting, stopping or paused

post.summary:
Export a stopped machine to a `.smolmachine` and push it directly to a
registry.
post.description:
The machine must be stopped: exporting a running VM would snapshot an
inconsistent overlay. The `.smolmachine` is produced by subprocessing this
same binary's `pack create --from-vm <name>` (the tested path that boots a
helper VM to export the container overlay), then streamed to the registry
with the control-plane-minted, pre-scoped OCI bearer.

409.description: Machine is not stopped

get.summary:
Report live node capacity — current allocations + real utilization across
all running machines on this host.
get.description:
Read-only and runtime-agnostic: it exposes only what the runtime knows
(allocated vs. used), leaving totals/reserved policy to the caller. A fleet
node-agent polls this over HTTP and forwards it to the control plane in its
heartbeat, which keeps the runtime itself free of any cloud coupling.

503.description: Main runtime stalled — node is unschedulable

get.summary: Health check endpoint.

AcquireForkLeaseBatchRequest.description: A bounded group of ordinary fork-pool lease requests.

leases.description:
Independent lease requests. Each item retains its normal idempotency semantics;
at most 32 items may wait for workload readiness in one call.

AcquireForkLeaseBatchResponse.description: Ordered results from a bounded fork-pool lease batch.

leases.description: One result per submitted lease request, in input order.

AcquireForkLeaseRequest.description: Request to acquire one clean worker from a fork pool.

awaitWorkerReady.description: Keep the lease activating until the workload calls `smolvm-worker-ready`.

env.description: Job-specific KEY=VALUE parameters installed before the workload runs.

files.description:
Small files written atomically under `/workspace` before the workload is
released. The entire worker is discarded if any file cannot be staged.

idempotencyKey.description: Retry key unique within the pool. Repeating it returns the same lease.

oneOf.description: Optional fused-rollout access granted only to this lease's executor and policy.

ttlSecs.description: Optional lease duration override for this worker.

waitSecs.description:
Wait up to this many seconds for a clean worker when none is ready,
instead of failing with 503 right away. Defaults to 0 (no wait). The
acquisition request can remain open for this duration, so clients must
use a longer request deadline.

workerReadyTimeoutSecs.description:
Optional readiness timeout in seconds; defaults to 240 when enabled. The
acquisition request can remain open for this duration, so clients must use
a longer request deadline.

BlockIoEngine.description:
Host engine used to service guest block-device requests.

Synchronous I/O is the compatibility default and has no asynchronous
setup cost. The asynchronous engine is an explicit Linux optimization that
overlaps queued raw-disk reads through a restricted io_uring; buffered
writes stay inline.

CacheDiskSpec.description:
A shared cache disk: a read-only base image the machine reads through its
own copy-on-write layer, mounted at `mountPath`. Many machines start from
one base without writing to it, and every branch gets its own layer.

base.description:
File name of the base image in the server's cache disk directory
(`smolvm serve --cache-disk-dir`). A name, never a path.

mountPath.description: Absolute guest path the cache filesystem is mounted at.

slot.description:
Attach the cache disk as a slot: left unmounted, so a checkpoint of the
machine can later be restored with a different cache mounted here.

CapacityResponse.description:
Live node capacity: current allocations and real utilization across all
running machines on this host. Read-only introspection — a fleet control
plane (or any operator) polls this to gauge node load. The reporter owns
totals/reserved; this endpoint reports only what the runtime itself knows.

allocated_cpus.description: CPUs allocated to running machines (sum of per-machine cpu requests).

boot_id.description:
Opaque id minted once per serve process. It changes iff the serve restarts
— the signal the control uses to detect that this node's warm pool (and any
in-memory VM state) was wiped, so it can prune the now-stale pool records.

branch_child_growth_fraction.description:
Share of a child's guest RAM (0..=1) branch admission charges per child
on top of `branch_child_overhead_mb`, for the pages it dirties later.

branch_child_overhead_mb.description: Boot overhead (MB) branch admission charges per child on this node.

branch_growth_owed_mb.description:
Growth (MB) branch admission has promised running branch children and
they have not yet taken: each child's charge less its private memory
now. Branch admission holds it back from `host_memory_available_mb`.

branch_reserve_mb.description:
Host memory (MB) a branch must leave free on this node. A branch of N
children is refused unless `host_memory_available_mb`, less
`branch_growth_owed_mb`, covers this plus
`N * (branch_child_overhead_mb + branch_child_growth_fraction * the
source's guest RAM)` plus any fresh RAM generation it copies.
Omitted when branch memory admission is off or host memory is unknown.

checkpoint_store_bytes.description:
Disk space (bytes) the node's incremental checkpoint store held at its
last retention run. Omitted until one has run.

cuda_devices.description:
CUDA devices currently visible to this runtime. Omitted when NVML is
unavailable, no CUDA device is visible, or the latest sample failed.
Device ordinals use the same CUDA-visible ordering as
`SMOLVM_CUDA_DEVICE` and fork-pool admission.

host_memory_available_mb.description: Effective memory currently available (MB) to this runtime.

host_memory_total_mb.description:
Effective memory ceiling (MB) available to this runtime, constrained by
finite cgroup-v2 ancestors where applicable.

used_cpus.description: Real fractional CPU load across VM processes (e.g. 2.5 = 2.5 CPUs).

used_disk_gb.description: Real disk (GB) consumed by VM storage + overlay files.

used_memory_mb.description: Real resident memory (MB) across VM processes.

used_memory_private_mb.description: Private resident memory (MB) across VM processes.

used_memory_pss_mb.description:
Proportional resident memory (MB) across VM processes. Unlike summed
RSS, this counts clean pages shared by branch siblings only once in the
aggregate. Omitted: `/capacity` sums the kernel's cheap per-process
counters, which carry no PSS, because summing `smaps_rollup` over every
machine outlasts the node-agent's poll. A machine's own usage reports it.

used_memory_shared_mapped_mb.description:
Sum of shared bytes mapped by VM processes (MB). This is a mapping gauge,
not a unique physical-memory total; use `used_memory_pss_mb` for that.

oneOf.description: Program and arguments.
A shell command line.

CommandSpec.description:
A command as the smol cloud API takes it: an argument list, or one string
run with `sh -lc`.

CreateExecSessionRequest.description:
Start a command the node owns: it outlives the request that started it,
keeps its output for readers to fetch by offset, and keeps its exit code
until read. See `api::exec_sessions`.

Same command fields as [`ExecRequest`], plus the session's id and shape.

autoStart.description: Boot a stopped machine to run the command (the default).

command.description: Command and arguments, or one string run with `sh -lc`.

env.description:
Environment variables by name. A list of `{name, value}` is also
accepted.

execId.description:
The session's id, 8 to 64 of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`. A client chooses it so a
retried start finds the session the first one made instead of running
the command twice. Generated when absent.

interactive.description:
Stdin stays open for sequenced frames (`POST .../stdin` or the attach
WebSocket). An interactive session left without a reader for the
detach grace is killed.

maxBytes.description: Most output bytes in the answer.

secrets.description: Ad-hoc secret refs; rejected unless empty (see [`ExecRequest`]).

stdin.description:
Data written to the command's stdin when it starts. Unless
`interactive`, stdin is closed after it.

timeoutSeconds.description:
Kill the command after this many seconds (exit code 124;
`timeoutSecs` is accepted too).

tty.description: Run the command on a PTY (implies `interactive`); stderr joins stdout.

waitSeconds.description:
Wait up to this many seconds (at most 60) for output or the exit before
answering, and answer with the output from offset 0; a short command
then needs this one request (`waitSecs` is accepted too).

CreateForkPoolRequest.description: Request to create an automatically replenished pool of held fork workers.

autoAdmission.description:
Automatically calibrate resident CUDA leases. Defaults on for shared
CUDA pools when omitted; set false for full residency.

desiredReady.description: Number of clean workers kept booted and ready.

freezeSource.description: Keep the source paused while this pool is replenished from its checkpoint.

leaseTtlSecs.description: Default seconds an acquired worker may run without a heartbeat.

maxActive.description: Optional maximum number of simultaneously active leases.

readyTimeoutSecs.description: Maximum seconds to wait for the golden workload forkpoint.

shareWeights.description: Share immutable CUDA allocations with the golden and sibling workers.

source.description: Existing running branchable machine whose workload is at the branch point.

CreateMachineRequest.description:
Request to create a new machine.

`deny_unknown_fields`: create carries the machine's security posture
(`allowedCidrs`, `allowedHosts`, `credentials`, `networkBackend`), and a
misspelled or mis-cased entry used to be dropped silently, yielding a
machine with wider network access than the caller asked for. Same rule as
`ExecRequest`, and it applies to the nested specs too, so a typo inside
`restart` or `mounts` is also a hard 400.

allowedHosts.description:
Allowed egress hostnames (and their subdomains); DNS answers for these
names are learned into the egress allow-list.

autoGraph.description:
Ask compatible CUDA frameworks to graph safe compiled regions.
Implies CUDA; arbitrary eager CUDA calls are not captured.

blobPeers.description:
Brokered P2P blob peers: node base URLs (`https://<addr>:<port>`) supplied
by the control plane. On a cache miss the layer blob is fetched from a
peer's `GET /p2p/blob/<digest>` (over node→node mTLS) before the registry.
Empty (the default) ⇒ registry-only, byte-for-byte as before.

oneOf.description: Host block I/O engine. `sync` is the default; `async` is opt-in.

Shared cache disk: a base from the server's cache disk directory,
mounted through the machine's own copy-on-write layer. Not allowed when
restoring a checkpoint, which keeps the disks it was captured with.

cmd.description: Workload command run when the machine starts (see `entrypoint`).

credentials.description:
Credential bindings substituted by the host on the way out (see
`ResourceSpec::credentials`). Placeholders replace the values in the
workload environment; the request never carries a credential value.

cuda.description: Enable CUDA remoting (host NVIDIA GPU via the bundled shims).

oneOf.description:
When guest disk writes must reach the host's disk: `full` (default)
or `deferred`.

diskVolumes.description:
Guest paths kept on the machine's storage disk instead of its overlay
root, like Docker's anonymous volume `-v /var/lib/docker` (the CLI's
`-v PATH` with no host side). Put a nested container engine's data root
here so it can use overlayfs instead of falling back to vfs.

dockerSocket.description:
Expose the guest's Docker daemon socket to the host as a Unix socket in
the VM data dir, so a host client can drive it with `DOCKER_HOST=unix://…`.
Off by default.

entrypoint.description:
Workload entrypoint. With `cmd`, overrides the image's (or the
`.smolmachine` artifact's) own entrypoint+cmd, matching the CLI's
`machine create -- <command>` precedence. Empty = use the image's.

env.description:
Environment variables for the machine's workload (init commands and the
entrypoint). For `from`/`registry_ref` machines these layer on top of
the artifact manifest's env; a request variable wins on name collision.

from.description:
Path to a `.smolmachine` or `.checkpoint` artifact. Creates from
pre-packed layers or restores the artifact's captured live state.
Mutually exclusive with `image`.

guestSubnet.description:
IPv4 subnet the guest link is drawn from (virtio-net only), e.g.
`10.200.0.0/30`. The gateway and the guest's resolver take the first host
address and the guest the second. Omit for the default `100.96.0.0/30`,
which collides with Tailscale or carrier NAT running inside the guest.

image.description:
OCI image reference (e.g., "alpine:latest"), or a `docker save` / OCI
archive or rootfs directory under the server's `--local-image-dir`.
Mutually exclusive with `from`.

nestedVirt.description:
Expose the host's virtualization extensions so the guest can run its own
VMs (nested KVM). Refused with 403 unless the server runs with
`--allow-nested-virt`; it hands the guest the host kernel's nested-KVM
code, so enable it only for trusted workloads.

network.description:
Enable outbound network access (TSI).
Note: Only TCP/UDP supported, not ICMP (ping).

oneOf.description:
Network backend: `tsi` (outbound-only) or `virtio-net`.

When omitted, machines created through the API default to `virtio-net`:
the server configures a guest host-service (the rollout ingress), and
published `ports`, egress policies and fleet mode need virtio-net too.
(`tsi` is the default only for outbound-only machines launched outside
`smolvm serve`.) Set `tsi` explicitly for the lighter outbound-only
backend; published `ports` require `virtio-net` (TSI has no inbound
path), so that combination is rejected.

registryIdentityToken.description:
Bearer credential (an OCI Distribution `identity_token`) to present when
pulling `registry_ref`. The control plane supplies a short-lived,
tenant-scoped token here so a node can fetch a tenant's private
`.smolmachine`. Takes precedence over any persisted registry credential.

registryRef.description:
Registry reference to a .smolmachine artifact (e.g., "myapp:v1").
Pulls from the registry before creating the VM.
Mutually exclusive with `image` and `from`.

oneOf.description: Restart policy configuration.

secrets.description:
Secret refs attached to the machine. Resolved at every
subsequent exec against the host's env/files. Rejected unless empty;
accepted — `from_env`/`from_file` on the API surface would let
an untrusted caller exfiltrate the server process's env or
read arbitrary host files; use the CLI `machine create` path
for those source kinds.

stopSignal.description:
Signal sent to the workload when the machine stops, so it can save its
state and exit: a name such as `SIGINT` or `SIGRTMIN+3`, or a number.
Default `SIGTERM`.

stopTimeoutSecs.description:
Seconds the workload gets to exit after its stop signal before it is
killed. Default 10, at most 300.

workdir.description:
Working directory for the machine's workload. Overrides the artifact
manifest's workdir when set.

CreateRolloutExecutorRequest.description: Request to register one local fused rollout engine.

adapterRoot.description: Host directory beneath which adapter paths must resolve.

backend.description: Backend kind. Only `vllm` is currently supported.

deviceAdapterSocket.description: Optional private Unix socket for device-resident LoRA handoff without host staging.

endpoint.description: Loopback HTTP endpoint of the backend, for example `http://127.0.0.1:8000`.

fallbackPool.description: Optional ordinary fork pool used by framework adapters as a compatibility fallback.

maxQueueDepth.description: Maximum requests waiting behind active work.

requestTimeoutSecs.description: Whole-request deadline used when a caller supplies no shorter deadline.

CredentialBindingsRequest.description: Request to replace a machine's credential bindings (`PUT /api/v1/machines/{name}/credential-bindings`).

credentials.description:
The machine's bindings after the change: kept ones keep their placeholders, added ones get new ones, and any
left out are removed.

atNextStart.description: The machine runs but booted without bindings: they apply from its next start.

live.description: The running machine uses them from its next request.

CredentialValuesRequest.description:
Values for a machine's credential bindings, by binding name.

Held in the server's memory only — never written to the machine record,
a checkpoint or disk — and applied at the machine's next boot (start,
resume or restore). A server restart forgets them, so supply them again
before each start. A machine whose bindings came in over this API resolves
them from here and nowhere else.

values.description:
Binding name → value. Replaces whatever was supplied before; empty
clears it.

CudaDeviceCapacity.description: Live capacity and identity for one host CUDA device.

memoryFreeMib.description: Current free device memory in MiB.

ordinal.description: CUDA-visible ordinal used to assign a machine or pool to this device.

uuid.description: Stable NVIDIA GPU or MIG UUID.

DeleteForkPoolQuery.description: Query parameters for deleting a fork pool.

force.description: Cancel active leases and delete their workers as well.

DeleteQuery.description: Query parameters for delete machine endpoint.

cascade.description:
If true, also delete any clones forked from this machine before removing
it. A fork base cannot be removed while its clones' overlays depend on
its disks; cascade removes those clones first. Default: false.

force.description:
If true, force delete even if stop fails and VM is still running.
This may orphan the VM process. Default: false.

DiskDurability.description:
When a guest's disk writes must reach the host's physical disk.

`Full`: an `fsync` in the guest returns only once the host has flushed the
write to its physical disk, so a commit survives a host crash. `Deferred`:
a guest `fsync` still writes everything out to the machine's disk files, so
the machine, a restart, a checkpoint and a branch all see it, but it does
not wait for the physical disk; the host kernel writes it back on its own
schedule, and a host crash can lose recent writes. For machines whose state
is disposable (tests, rollouts), that turns fsync-bound work such as
database commits from a disk round trip into a memory copy. The guest sees
the same disk either way, so a checkpoint restores under either setting.

EgressDenialInfo.description:
One egress denial: the machine's egress policy refused an outbound
connect or sendto. These are the machine's only record of blocked
traffic, read from the VMM's log.

dest.description: The destination the guest tried to reach.

timestamp.description:
Denial time (RFC 3339, microsecond precision), or empty when the
log line carried no parseable timestamp.

events.description: Denials oldest-first, capped by the `limit` query parameter.

EgressFlowSummary.description:
Open TCP flows of a running machine, as last flushed by its network stack.
Outbound flows are the guest's own connections; inbound ones arrived on a
published port.

distinctOutboundPeers.description: Distinct destination IPs among the open outbound flows.

oldestOutboundDest.description: `ip:port` of the longest-lived open outbound flow.

oldestOutboundSecs.description:
Age in seconds, as of `updatedAt`, of the longest-lived open outbound
flow; 0 when there is none.

EgressSignal.description:
Matches against the operator's egress watchlist for one label and
destination, summarized from the machine's signal log.

at.description: Latest time it was recorded, in the same form as `first_at`.

count.description:
How many times it was recorded in the recent log. A repeat within a
minute is recorded once, so this counts minutes with activity, roughly.

dest.description:
What matched: the name asked in a DNS question or a TLS ClientHello,
or `ip:port`.

firstAt.description:
First time it was recorded (RFC 3339), or empty when the line carried
no parseable timestamp.

label.description:
The watchlist entry's label, as written in the watchlist file, or
`stratum` for a miner's pool login.

ExecOutputChunk.description: One piece of an exec session's output.

offset.description: Offset of the first byte. Stdout and stderr share one offset space.

ExecOutputGap.description:
Offsets a reader asked for that the node no longer holds: it fell more
than the output window behind after being away longer than the detach
grace.

ExecRequest.description:
Request to execute a command in a machine.

Field names and shapes follow the smol cloud API (`cwd`, `timeoutSeconds`,
`env` as an object, `command` as a list or one shell string); the older
`workdir`, `timeoutSecs` and `env` list are still accepted.

`deny_unknown_fields`: an unknown or mis-cased field is a hard 400, not a
silent no-op. This matters for the safety fields (`timeoutSeconds`, etc.) —
a caller who writes `timeout_seconds` must be told, not left running an
untrusted command with no timeout because the field was quietly dropped.

autoStart.description:
Boot a stopped machine to run the command (the default). `false` answers
409 instead, for a caller that must reach only a machine already running,
such as a readiness probe that would otherwise wake one stopped meanwhile.

background.description:
Run the command detached: spawn it in the background and return its PID
immediately instead of waiting. The process keeps running (a long-lived
daemon — dev server, agent runner) until it exits or the machine stops.

command.description: Command and arguments, or one string run with `sh -lc`.

env.description:
Environment variables by name. A list of `{name, value}` is also
accepted.

secrets.description:
Ad-hoc secret refs. Rejected unless empty: an untrusted HTTP
caller cannot read this host's env/files. See `RequestSecretRefs`.

stdin.description: Data to pipe to the command's stdin.

stream.description:
Stream stdout and stderr as Server-Sent Events, as
`POST .../exec/stream` does, instead of one JSON body.

timeoutSeconds.description: Timeout in seconds (`timeoutSecs` is accepted too).

user.description:
Run as this user: a name from the image or a numeric `uid[:gid]`,
overriding the image's USER. Only meaningful for image machines; a bare
VM has no container user to become.

ExecResponse.description:
Command execution result.

**Encoding note**: `stdout`/`stderr` are a lossy UTF-8 view (non-UTF-8 bytes
become U+FFFD) kept for older clients. `stdoutB64`/`stderrB64` carry the raw,
byte-exact output (base64) and should be preferred by callers that need
binary-safe results (image bytes, tarballs, etc.) — the agent preserves
bytes end-to-end and these fields do too.

stderr.description: Standard error, lossy UTF-8 (non-UTF-8 bytes → U+FFFD). Prefer `stderrB64`.

stderrB64.description: Raw stderr bytes, base64-encoded — byte-exact, binary-safe.

stdout.description: Standard output, lossy UTF-8 (non-UTF-8 bytes → U+FFFD). Prefer `stdoutB64`.

stdoutB64.description: Raw stdout bytes, base64-encoded — byte-exact, binary-safe.

ExecSessionReadQuery.description: Query for reading an exec session's output.

after.description:
Return output from this offset. It also acknowledges every byte before
it, which the node then drops. Default 0.

max.description: Most output bytes in the answer.

wait.description:
Wait up to this many seconds (at most 60) for output past `after` or
the exit. Default 0.

ExecSessionResponse.description: An exec session's state and the output a read returned.

done.description:
The command ended and `output` reaches the end of its output: nothing
more will come. Stop reading here.

end.description: One past the newest byte produced.

error.description:
Why the session ended without an exit code (killed, the machine
stopped, it never started), or what went wrong around it.

exitCode.description: The command's exit code, once it exited.

oneOf.description: Offsets asked for that are no longer held.

next.description: Pass as `after` on the next read.

output.description: Output after the offset asked for, in offset order.

start.description: The oldest offset the node still holds.

stdinApplied.description: The last stdin frame applied (0 = none).

ExecStdinRequest.description: One stdin frame for an interactive exec session.

data.description: The bytes, base64-encoded, at most 64 KiB.

seq.description:
The frame's sequence number; the first is 1. A frame applies only after
the one before it; a frame already applied is acknowledged and ignored.

ExportRequest.description:
Request to export a stopped machine to a `.smolmachine` and push it to a
registry. The control plane mints a pre-scoped OCI bearer (`push_token`)
that authorizes the write against `reference_host`.

pushToken.description: Pre-scoped OCI bearer token minted by the control plane.

ExportResponse.description: Result of exporting a machine to a registry.

digest.description: Digest of the pushed OCI manifest (reference as `repo@<digest>`).

manifest.description: The `PackManifest` JSON carried in the sidecar footer.

sizeBytes.description: Size of the `.smolmachine` sidecar blob in bytes.

ExternalInterceptorSpec.description: Host interceptor binding supplied in a machine start request.

mediated.description: Use the versioned mediated protocol with host-minted launch identity.

token.description: Authentication token shared with the interceptor, as 64 hex digits.

path.description: Path where the file was written.

size.description: Size of the file in bytes.

ForkLeaseBatchItemResponse.description: One ordered result from a fork-pool lease batch.

errorCode.description: Stable API error category when this item failed.

idempotencyKey.description: Retry key from the submitted lease request.

oneOf.description: Activated worker lease when acquisition succeeded.

ForkLeaseInfo.description: Public state of one one-shot fork worker lease.

createdAt.description: Unix timestamp when the lease was acquired.

expiresAt.description: Unix timestamp after which a missing heartbeat retires the worker.

id.description: Opaque lease identifier used for heartbeat and completion.

machine.description: Machine name usable with existing exec, file, and log APIs.

state.description: Lease state: activating, active, completed, expired, failed, or cancelled.

ForkLeasePayloadFile.description: One file staged into a held worker before lease activation.

mode.description: Optional Unix permission bits in decimal; defaults to 420 (`0644`).

ForkPoolInfo.description: Current size and lifecycle state of an automatic fork pool.

activating.description: Workers durably claimed while guest release is in progress.

active.description: Workers currently owned by active leases.

admissionCalibrating.description: True while the controller is comparing resident levels.

admissionReason.description: Human-readable reason for the current automatic limit.

autoAdmission.description: Whether lease residency is calibrated automatically.

createdAt.description: Unix timestamp when the pool was created.

cudaDeviceOrdinal.description: Host CUDA device inherited from the pool golden.

deleting.description: True after asynchronous deletion has begun.

effectiveActiveLimit.description: Current dynamic resident limit when automatic admission is enabled.

effectiveDeviceLimit.description: Aggregate dynamic resident limit shared by pools on this CUDA device.

freezeSource.description: Whether this pool keeps its source paused for repeated branches.

gpuMemoryTotalMib.description: Memory capacity of this pool's CUDA device in MiB.

gpuMemoryUsedMib.description: Latest memory use on this pool's CUDA device in MiB.

gpuUtilizationPercent.description: Latest utilization of this pool's CUDA device.

hostCpuPercent.description: Latest host CPU busy percentage used by admission.

provisioning.description: Workers still being forked and booted.

ready.description: Clean held workers immediately available for acquisition.

retiring.description: Workers being destroyed before replacement or pool deletion.

shareWeights.description: Whether immutable CUDA allocations are shared.

ForkReleaseRequest.description: Assignment for one already-booted held fork slot.

env.description:
Job-specific KEY=VALUE parameters. A value replaces a same-named value
installed while provisioning the slot.

ForkRequest.description: Request to branch a running, branchable source machine into a new child.

env.description:
Per-fork parameters as KEY=VALUE strings. Delivered to the clone at
`/etc/smolvm/fork-env` (dotenv format) for the already-running workload
to read, and merged into the clone's env for later exec sessions.

freezeSource.description: Keep the source paused as a reusable branch base.

hold.description:
Keep the clone parked at the inherited forkpoint as an already-booted
pool slot. Implies `waitReady`; release it exactly once through the
fork-release endpoint after assigning job-specific parameters.

keepMachineId.description:
Keep the source's `/etc/machine-id` (and dbus id) in the clone instead
of minting a fresh one. Hostname, SSH host keys and cloud-init state are
still re-minted. For same-tenant fan-out whose tools key a per-machine
cache by machine id (Nx names its cache database after it), so a warm
source's cache stays visible in every clone.

labels.description: Labels set on the child over the ones inherited from the source.

name.description: Name for the new child machine.

ports.description:
Pin the clone's inbound port forwards. Without this, the golden's
forwards are remapped to freshly-allocated host ports so the clone does
not collide with the still-running golden or sibling clones.

readyTimeoutSecs.description:
Maximum seconds to wait for the golden workload's forkpoint. Defaults
to 240 when `waitReady` or `hold` is enabled.

secrets.description:
Per-fork secrets as `SecretRef`s (host env var / absolute file). Merged
into the clone's persisted `secret_refs`, overriding same-named refs
inherited from the golden — so each clone gets its OWN secrets, resolved
fresh on every `exec`, never written to the overlay/artifact or a guest
file, and isolated from the golden and sibling clones. This is the
fork-safe path: unlike `env`, the plaintext never lands at rest.

shareWeights.description:
Share the golden's loaded CUDA weights with this clone instead of
copying them (one base copy in VRAM across sibling clones). Correct when
the base stays frozen (LoRA/QLoRA fine-tuning, inference).

waitReady.description:
Wait for the workload's standard forkpoint before snapshotting, then
release the clone only after identity and fork parameters are installed.

GuestPressure.description:
Pressure stall information of a running machine's guest, from
`/proc/pressure/{cpu,memory,io}` inside it, refreshed about every 15 s.

cpu.description: Time tasks waited for a CPU.

io.description: Time tasks waited for block IO.

memory.description: Time tasks waited for memory: reclaim, swap and refaults.

checkpoint_device_profiles.description:
Checkpoint device profiles this engine can read. Capacity, architecture,
CPU features, and runtime compatibility are checked separately.

checkpoint_format_versions.description: Portable-checkpoint metadata formats understood by the reader.

oneOf.description: Machine counts.

nested_virt.description:
Whether this server runs nested-virtualization machines (started with
`--allow-nested-virt`), so a fleet scheduler can place them here.

ListExecSessionsResponse.description: The exec sessions on a machine.

ListForkPoolsResponse.description: List response for automatic fork pools.

after.description:
Resume from this file offset: the `id` of the last event received.
The SSE `Last-Event-ID` header does the same. Every event of a resumed
read carries the offset just past its line as its `id`.

follow.description: If true, follow the logs (like tail -f). Default: false.

format.description: Output format: "raw" (default) or "json" (only emit valid JSON lines).

ids.description:
Give every event the offset just past its line as its `id`, so the
read can be resumed with `after`.

source.description:
Which log: "console" (default), the machine's agent and kernel
console, or "workload", its workload's stdout and stderr, which is
kept across restarts and readable while the machine is stopped.

tail.description: Number of lines to show from the end (like tail -n). Default: all.

allowedCidrs.description: Allowed egress CIDRs. Omitted when unrestricted; an empty list denies all.

allowedHosts.description: Allowed egress hostnames. Omitted when unset. Echoes back what `create` accepted.

blockIo.description: Host block I/O engine used by this machine.

branchable.description:
Whether this machine can be branched as it is: how it was launched while
it runs (a plain-created machine started with `branchable` is one, a
branchable-created one started plain is not), else whether an ordinary
start launches it as a branch source.

branchpointHeld.description:
True while this child is an already-booted clean slot parked at the
workload branchpoint and available for one assignment.

oneOf.description: The machine's shared cache disk, its base named by file name.

cpuLimitMillicpus.description:
CPU limit in force on the running VMM, in milli-CPUs across all vCPUs,
set with `PUT /machines/{name}/cpu-limit` and reapplied on every later
launch until cleared. Omitted when none is set or the machine is stopped.

cpuMillis.description:
Same consumed CPU but in MILLISECONDS — sub-second precision so consumers
integrating this don't quantize a barely-busy process up to a whole second.
Derived from the same nanosecond sample as `cpu_seconds`. Omitted for
stopped machines (no live process to sample).

cpuSeconds.description:
Consumed CPU-seconds (user+system) of the machine's CURRENT VMM process,
sampled live from the host. Resets to 0 on a VM restart — it's a stateless
snapshot; the control plane accumulates a durable total from it. Omitted
for stopped machines (no live process to sample).

cuda.description: Whether transparent CUDA remoting is enabled for this machine.

cudaBranchPoolSize.description: Planned runnable CUDA child count used for automatic capacity budgeting.

cudaVramLimitMib.description: Explicit logical CUDA memory limit per source/child session, in MiB.

diskChainDepth.description:
Maximum number of backing layers across storage, overlay and cache disks.
Measured on machine detail requests; omitted when unavailable. A raw or
standalone disk has depth zero. This is not the branch generation.

diskDurability.description: When this machine's guest disk writes must reach the host's disk.

diskUsedMb.description:
Actual host disk consumed by this machine's data dir, in MiB (real blocks of
the sparse disk images, not provisioned capacity). An instantaneous gauge the
control integrates over time for active-disk billing. Omitted when the data
dir can't be read.

diskVolumes.description: Guest paths kept on the machine's storage disk.

egressBytes.description:
Cumulative guest-outbound (egress) bytes since boot, for billing. Present
only for virtio-net machines that have reported a value; omitted for TSI
or machines that haven't flushed yet. Surfaced the same way `storage_gb`
is, so the control plane reads both from the machine list.

oneOf.description:
Open TCP flows of a running virtio-net machine, from the host-side
network stack's flow table, refreshed about every 15 s. Omitted for TSI
machines, stopped machines, and a summary older than two minutes.

egressSignals.description:
Matches against the operator's egress watchlist (`smolvm serve
--egress-watchlist`), and stratum handshakes under the built-in label
`stratum` (a miner logging in to its pool, whatever the pool), grouped
by label and destination, latest first. Omitted when there are none. Recorded by the host-side network stack the
guest cannot reach, for virtio-net machines.

gpu.description: Whether Vulkan/graphics GPU acceleration is enabled for this machine.

image.description: Resolved workload image, used to bind registry credentials to its host.

labels.description:
Labels: metadata to find and group machines by, as the cloud API
answers them.

mediationMachineId.description:
Host-minted identity of this launch, as carried by mediated egress
decisions (`machineId`), so a decider can map flows to the machine up
front. Present only while a mediated-egress machine is running.

mounts.description: Configured mounts (with virtiofs tags for container use).

network.description: Whether outbound network access is enabled.

oneOf.description:
Network backend the machine runs (`tsi` or `virtio-net`). Echoes back
what `create` accepted; omitted when `create` left it unset (the
launch then picks the contextual default — `virtio-net` under
`smolvm serve`, with ports, or with an egress policy; `tsi` otherwise).

parentMachine.description: Immediate parent machine when this machine was created by branching.

oneOf.description:
Pressure stall information from inside the guest
(`/proc/pressure/{cpu,memory,io}`), refreshed about every 15 s: how
much of the time tasks waited for CPU, memory or IO, which the host's
view of the VMM process cannot tell. Omitted for stopped machines,
before the first sample, for a guest kernel without PSI, and for a
sample older than two minutes.

pssMb.description:
Proportional resident memory (PSS) in MiB. Summing this across branch
siblings accounts shared clean pages once instead of once per sibling.

rssMb.description:
Current resident memory (RSS) of the machine's VMM process, in MiB, sampled
live from the host. Unlike CPU this is an instantaneous gauge (not a
counter); the control plane integrates it over time for active-memory
billing. Omitted for stopped machines (no live process to sample).

oneOf.description: Process identity for conditional live mutations; absent when unavailable.

sharedMemoryMappedMb.description:
Shared memory mapped by this VMM in MiB. This is not a unique physical
total when summed; use PSS for physical accounting.

stateReason.description:
Why the host put the machine in this state when it was not the user:
a branch child the memory pressure guard paused says so here.

MachineMetricsResponse.description:
One reading of a machine's resource use (`GET /api/v1/machines/{name}/metrics`),
in the shape the cloud API answers it.

CPU is a counter: utilization over an interval is the change in
`cpuMillis` divided by the elapsed milliseconds times `vcpus`. The counter
starts again at 0 when the machine's VM restarts. Readings are present only
while the machine runs.

at.description: When the readings were taken, RFC 3339 with milliseconds.

cpuLimitMillicpus.description: A CPU limit in force right now, in thousandths of a CPU.

cpuMillis.description: CPU time the machine has used since its VM started, in milliseconds.

diskUsedMb.description: Disk space in use in MiB.

egressBytes.description: Bytes the machine has sent out since its VM started.

machineId.description: The machine these readings are for.

memoryLimitMb.description: The machine's memory size in MiB.

memoryMb.description: Memory in use in MiB, with pages shared with branches split among them.

oneOf.description: How much of recent time tasks in the guest waited for CPU, memory or IO.

rssMb.description: Resident memory in MiB, counting shared pages in full.

MachinePressure.description: Pressure stall readings from inside the guest.

cpu.description: Time tasks waited for a CPU.

io.description: Time tasks waited for block IO.

machineId.description: Host-minted identity for this VM launch.

parentId.description: Host-minted identity of the branch source, or all zeros.

reason.description: Local policy, broker decision, or broker unavailability.

timestampMs.description: Unix epoch milliseconds when the decision was recorded.

MediationEventsResponse.description: Bounded list of mediated egress decisions.

events.description: Events oldest-first, capped by the `limit` query parameter.

MountInfo.description: Mount information (for responses, includes virtiofs tag).

staged.description: Whether this is a guest-local staged mount.

tag.description: Virtiofs tag (e.g., "smolvm0"). Use this in container mounts.

staged.description: Use a guest-local working copy and synchronize it in batches.

NetworkBackend.description: Network backend override for machine launch.

protocol.description:
Transport to forward: `tcp` (the default) or `udp`. A UDP port is
forwarded per remote client, and the machine answers each client
through the same host port.

PressureReading.description:
Percent of recent time at least one task (`some`) or every task (`full`)
waited for a resource.

fullAvg10.description: Over the last 10 seconds; always 0 for CPU.

fullAvg60.description: Over the last 60 seconds; always 0 for CPU.

PressureStall.description:
The guest's pressure stall information, as last sampled from its kernel.

Each resource carries the kernel's `some` and `full` shares (percent over
the last 10, 60 and 300 seconds) and the stalled time since boot in
microseconds, so a reader keeping samples can compute the share over its
own window from the totals.

fullAvg10.description:
Share of the last 10 s with every task stalled, in percent. Always 0
for CPU.

fullAvg300.description: Share of the last 300 s with every task stalled, in percent.

fullAvg60.description: Share of the last 60 s with every task stalled, in percent.

fullTotalUs.description: Microseconds since boot with every task stalled.

someAvg10.description: Share of the last 10 s with at least one task stalled, in percent.

someAvg300.description: Share of the last 300 s with at least one task stalled, in percent.

someAvg60.description: Share of the last 60 s with at least one task stalled, in percent.

someTotalUs.description: Microseconds since boot with at least one task stalled.

PublishCacheDiskRequest.description: Publish a stopped machine's cache disk as a new base.

base.description:
File name for the new base in the server's cache disk directory. Bases
are immutable: an existing name is refused, so publish each version
under a new one.

uploadUrls.description:
Also upload the new base to these pre-signed object-store URLs, one
contiguous part per URL, before answering.

base.description: File name of the new base in the server's cache disk directory.

sha256.description: SHA-256 (hex) of the new base, to verify a later fetch of it.

sizeBytes.description: Bytes the new base occupies on disk.

PublishDeviceRolloutPolicyRequest.description: Request to publish one immutable LoRA policy directly from clone GPU memory.

retainPrevious.description: Keep the previous current version routable instead of retiring it.

tensorBundleToken.description: Hex-encoded one-use token returned by the clone's CUDA publisher.

version.description: Immutable version identifier, normally the optimizer step.

PublishRolloutPolicyRequest.description: Request to publish one immutable LoRA policy version.

adapterPath.description: Relative directory beneath the executor's configured adapter root.

adapterSha256.description: Expected deterministic SHA-256 of the adapter directory contents.

retainPrevious.description: Keep the previous current version routable instead of retiring it.

version.description: Immutable version identifier, normally the optimizer step or content digest.

noProxy.description: Comma-separated NO_PROXY list of hosts/CIDRs that bypass the proxy.

proxy.description:
Proxy URL applied to the in-VM registry client
(sets HTTP_PROXY and HTTPS_PROXY).

RegistryAuthSpec.description:
Credentials for the registry a machine's image lives in.

Supplied per-start rather than stored on the machine record: a customer's
registry password must not be written to node disk, and the caller (the
control plane) already re-sends it on every dispatch. The username is
conventional for token-style credentials (`token`, `oauth2accesstoken`,
a GitHub PAT username); what matters is the password.

ResizeForkPoolRequest.description: Request to change a pool's clean-worker target.

desiredReady.description: New number of clean workers to keep booted and ready.

ResizeMachineRequest.description: Request to resize running CPU, RAM, or disk resources.

cpus.description: Target online CPU count; shrinking requires a compatible Linux x86_64 runtime and agent.

oneOf.description: Refuse growth if this observed runtime has exited or been replaced.

memoryMb.description: Total usable RAM allocation in MiB (live growth, optional).

operationId.description: Stable operation identity for safe retries; requires expectedRuntime.

overlayGb.description: Overlay disk size in GiB (expand only, optional).

storageGb.description: Storage disk size in GiB (expand only, optional).

allowedCidrs.description:
Allowed egress CIDR ranges. When set, only these IP ranges are reachable.
Omit for unrestricted egress. Empty list denies all egress.

allowedHosts.description:
Allowed egress hostnames. When set, DNS answers for these names (and their
subdomains) are learned into the egress allow-list so the machine can reach
them by name. Combine with `allowed_cidrs` to also permit fixed ranges.

oneOf.description:
Host block I/O engine. `sync` is the default; `async` submits queued raw-disk
reads through a restricted io_uring on Linux hosts.
Shared cache disk (see [`CacheDiskSpec`]).

credentials.description:
Credential bindings substituted by the host: the workload receives a
placeholder in each `environment_variable` and the real value is
injected only on HTTPS requests to that binding's `allowed_hosts`.
Values are never part of the request; the host resolves each binding
from its own secret store.

cuda.description:
Enable CUDA remoting (the guest sees the host NVIDIA GPU through the
bundled shims). Required on a golden that fork clones will train on.

oneOf.description:
When guest disk writes must reach the host's disk. `full` (the default)
makes a guest `fsync` wait for the host's physical disk. `deferred`
writes everything out to the machine's disks on `fsync` but does not
wait for the physical disk: much faster for fsync-heavy work such as
database commits, but a host crash can lose recent writes.

diskVolumes.description:
Guest paths kept on the machine's storage disk (see
`CreateMachineRequest::disk_volumes`).

egressRules.description: Ordered transport, CIDR and port rules applied before legacy egress policy.

guestSubnet.description:
IPv4 subnet the guest link is drawn from (virtio-net only), e.g.
`10.200.0.0/30`. The gateway and the guest's resolver take the first host
address and the guest the second. Omit for the default `100.96.0.0/30`,
which collides with Tailscale or carrier NAT running inside the guest.

nestedVirt.description:
Expose the host's virtualization extensions so the guest can run its own
VMs (nested KVM). Refused unless the server runs with
`--allow-nested-virt`; it hands the guest the host kernel's nested-KVM
code, so enable it only for trusted workloads.

network.description:
Enable outbound network access (TSI).
Note: Only TCP/UDP supported, not ICMP (ping).

oneOf.description:
Network backend: `tsi` (outbound-only) or `virtio-net`.

When omitted the backend is chosen from context: machines managed by
`smolvm serve` (every API machine), machines with published `ports`,
an egress policy (`allowedCidrs`/`allowedHosts`) or fleet mode default
to `virtio-net`; only outbound-only machines launched outside `serve`
(plain CLI) default to `tsi`. Set `tsi` explicitly to force the
lighter outbound-only backend (rejected alongside published `ports`).

RestartSpec.description: Restart policy specification for machine creation.

RolloutBatchItemResponse.description: One ordered item in a cohort response.

errorCode.description: Stable error category for a failed item.

idempotencyKey.description: Retry key from the submitted job.

oneOf.description: Successful result.

RolloutBatchRequest.description: A cohort of independent policy requests submitted together for backend fusion.

jobs.description: Independent generation jobs. Results retain this order.

RolloutBatchResponse.description: Ordered results for one submitted cohort.

RolloutCohort.description: A distributed batch boundary shared by independent rollout workers.

id.description: Unique identifier for one logical rollout round.

maxWaitMs.description: Optional bounded wait before the members already present are admitted.

size.description: Target number of independent jobs in this rollout round.

RolloutCompletion.description: One completion returned by the backend.

promptTokenIds.description: Exact prompt token IDs when supplied by the backend.

stopReason.description: Token or string that stopped generation.

tokenIds.description: Exact generated token IDs when supplied by the backend.

RolloutExecutorInfo.description: Runtime state and capabilities for one fused rollout engine.

accepting.description: Whether the executor accepts new publication and generation work.

capabilities.description: Backend capabilities understood by the stable API.

deviceAdapterSocket.description: Private device-adapter sidecar socket, when enabled.

queuedRequests.description: Requests currently waiting for an execution permit.

oneOf.description: Optional distributed admission cohort for independently submitted jobs.

idempotencyKey.description: Retry key unique within the executor.

prompts.description: Text or tokenized prompts. A request cannot mix the two representations.

version.description: Explicit immutable version, or the current version when omitted.

cached.description: True when an idempotent retry reused an earlier result.

RolloutLeaseAccess.description: Least-privilege fused-rollout scope injected into one pool worker.

executor.description: Existing rollout executor this worker may call.

policy.description: Logical policy this worker may publish, generate, and retire.

activeRequests.description: Requests using this version right now.

adapterSha256.description: Verified file-adapter digest or controller-derived device-publication digest.

backendModel.description: Opaque backend model name assigned by smolvm.

current.description: Whether this is the default version for the policy.

retiring.description: Whether this version is draining before backend unload.

text.description: Text prompt. Exactly one of `text` and `tokenIds` must be set.

tokenIds.description: Tokenized prompt. Exactly one of `text` and `tokenIds` must be set.

RolloutSamplingParams.description: Sampling parameters shared by every prompt in one request.

logprobs.description: Number of per-token alternatives to return.

RolloutUsage.description: Token accounting returned by a rollout backend.

RunRequest.description:
Request to run a command in an image.

`deny_unknown_fields`: like `ExecRequest`, a mis-cased safety field
(`timeout_secs` for `timeoutSecs`) is a 400, never a silent drop.

secrets.description: Ad-hoc secret refs. Rejected unless empty (untrusted scope).

user.description:
Run as this user: a name from the image or a numeric `uid[:gid]`,
overriding the image's USER.

RuntimeIdentity.description: Host process identity used to condition a mutation on the observed VMM.

bootId.description: Linux host boot identity; process start times are relative to this boot.

pid.description: Host process identifier; reuse is distinguished by its start time.

startTime.description: Platform-native process start timestamp, treated as an opaque value.

end.description: Bytes of output produced so far.

exitCode.description: The exit code, once it exited.

SetCpuLimitRequest.description: Request to set or clear a running machine's live CPU limit.

millicpus.description:
Host CPU the machine's VMM may use, in milli-CPUs across all its vCPUs
(200 = a fifth of one CPU), from 1 to vCPUs × 1000. `null` clears the
limit back to one CPU per vCPU. Required: an empty body is refused.
The guest still sees all its vCPUs, and the limit holds for every later
launch of the machine until cleared.

SetMachineEnvRequest.description:
Body of `PUT /api/v1/machines/{name}/env`: the machine's whole environment,
replacing what it had.

env.description:
Every variable the machine's commands start with, by name, as the
cloud API takes environment variables.

SetPortsRequest.description: Request to replace a machine's published ports.

ports.description:
The machine's published ports, the whole set; an empty list removes
them all. A running machine takes TCP changes now; its UDP ports stay
as they are until it stops.

branchPoolSize.description:
Number of runnable CUDA children planned for this source. Supplying it
enables branchable launch and transparent pre-initialization VRAM
budgeting for cache-sizing frameworks.

branchable.description:
Start as a branch source: back the guest RAM with a memfd (copy-on-write
cloneable) and expose a control socket so the machine can later be branched
with `POST /machines/{name}/branches`. Linux/x86_64 keeps the source running;
other hosts retain it as the frozen copy-on-write base.

cudaVramLimitMib.description: Explicit logical VRAM limit per source/child session, in MiB.

StartMachineRequest.description:
Optional body for `POST /machines/{name}/start`.

Entirely optional so an older caller that sends no body keeps working
unchanged — the route accepted only a query string before this existed.

Deliberately NOT `deny_unknown_fields`: the test below pins the contract
that unrelated JSON deserializes to "no credentials", so an older control
plane sending a newer body keeps starting machines.

branchPoolSize.description: The `branchPoolSize` query parameter, accepted in the body too.

branchable.description:
Start as a branch source; the same as the `branchable` query parameter,
so a caller that puts its start options in the body is not ignored.

cudaVramLimitMib.description: The `cudaVramLimitMib` query parameter, accepted in the body too.

oneOf.description:
External host egress interceptor for this start. The token remains on
the API server only and is never written to the machine record.

Credentials for the image's registry, used for THIS start only. Takes precedence over any registry credentials configured on the node, which are operator-level and therefore cannot be per-tenant. Without this, a private image on a third-party registry (a customer's own `ghcr.io//`) has no way to authenticate and the in-guest pull fails with an opaque DENIED.

UpdateEgressRequest.description:
Request to amend a machine's egress allow list: add or remove hosts,
patterns, and CIDRs without replacing the whole policy. The same merge and
guards as `machine update`, including on a running machine.

`deny_unknown_fields`: a mis-cased field on a security posture must be a
hard 400, never a silently dropped entry.

allowAll.description:
Permit a removal that empties the list, which allows egress to every
host. Mirrors `--net` on `machine update`.

allowHostPatterns.description: Patterns to allow: an exact hostname, or `*.domain` for subdomains only.

allowHosts.description: Hostnames to allow; each covers the name and its subdomains.

outboundLocalhostOnly.description:
Restrict outbound to localhost: adds `127.0.0.0/8` and `::1/128` to
the allowed CIDRs, as `--outbound-localhost-only` does.

removeAllowHosts.description: Allowed hostnames or patterns to remove, written as they were added.

resetAllowList.description:
Start from an empty allow list before applying this request's
additions, so the machine ends up with exactly what the request names.
A reset that names nothing needs `allowAll` to open egress. Cannot be
combined with removals. Mirrors `--reset-allow-list` on `machine update`.

UpdateMachineLabelsRequest.description:
Body of `PATCH /api/v1/machines/{name}/labels`: labels to change, leaving
the others as they are, as the cloud API takes them.

labels.description:
Labels to change: a string value sets or replaces that key, `null`
removes it (a key the machine does not carry is ignored). Keys left out
are untouched. The resulting set: at most 32; keys 1-63 chars of
`[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9._/-]*[a-z0-9])?`, values up to 255 chars.
